editor_note: Where it started: the first edition, twenty tracks, one rule — nothing you'd find on an algorithm's front page. Everything here was pulled from the week's writing around progressive rock and jazz-fusion, with the big names screened out. A proof of concept that grew legs.

spotify:track:52WF3uli6Aj23LZJH6LqNx.text: The Knifeworld/Cardiacs lineage at its most buoyant — Torabi's songcraft bends time signatures into pop shapes without ever losing the grin. A solo single that earned its opening slot.

spotify:track:0QWCGS1sD7StFSO36y4tiB.text: From the first harvest's deeper cuts — modern prog with a melodic heart and no interest in showing off.

spotify:track:59nNfTiRZVMJyU3efTJID2.text: Chicago's doom-psych heavyweights. Aerial Birth rides a riff the size of a weather system — the volume is the point, and the point is well taken.

spotify:track:4EfKHedelZj0Y6Mu5gFTkl.text: Quiet-loud dynamics done with actual feeling — Home builds its crescendo the old way, by earning it.

spotify:track:2Y0kBcHFWTPcZPTfFY4mR8.text: The French duo's single from Prog's Tracks Of The Week — angular, theatrical, unmistakably from the French prog tradition of taking odd ideas seriously.

spotify:track:3hl2iE2PJCtLcuGCzw2ZHS.text: Monumental in name and nature — modern prog with metal weight and architectural patience.

spotify:track:46pi0Hk8MwLED1NWz1OBbI.text: South American prog with real voltage — Abismo ("abyss") does exactly what the title promises.

spotify:track:4WlT2CKBDxLl0RL91Tz7f5.text: Piano-led fusion that whirls — the title is the honest review.

spotify:track:3G7vtEzg5JvWdvzR0UxBxr.text: One of the harvest's left-field picks — compact, hooky, and off-kilter in the right proportions.

spotify:track:2YF72dr6r89o9bS0x3Mabf.text: Drummer-led prog with aerial dynamics — OVERWHELMED wears its capital letters honestly.

spotify:track:7f8vi4dSKX2kD5z6H0cfkA.text: Italian post-sludge that swings for the horizon. The riff arrives like weather; Bring Down the Sky is the forecast.

spotify:track:0cEayj9GlWT2awWziRlOuL.text: The Neal Morse-adjacent outfit operating at full melodic strength — dream-logic prog with immaculate harmonies.

spotify:track:3HtMFY0vLnXjj7eXIvPEoA.text: Finnish prog metal with an unusually light touch for the genre — Illuminate glows rather than bludgeons.

spotify:track:1spN7elqO8ae86I2snOAiR.text: A pep talk with guitars — modern prog that takes its own advice.

spotify:track:34wkpfakN81SShZCdbtdWN.text: Brazilian jazz-fusion with a songwriter's wit — the escalator metaphor extends further than you'd think.

spotify:track:1K9sehA1QUYO5RfbGIRTCP.text: The Armenian pianist-composer's foliar arpeggios — a prelude that sounds like a whole orchestra tuning to a folk memory.

spotify:track:0aM1mCxoiwvhN5828gvLNV.text: Guitar-forward fusion with a romantic streak — Something To Believe In makes the case without words.

spotify:track:2UqXRWH0AO8l2ecr4C6cHS.text: A jazz-fusion two-hander with humor in the pocket — Matti's Mojo has the swing the name implies.

spotify:track:2NCKMGcBAK8C7QSA6C4sAQ.text: The Fugazi rhythm section's instrumental outfit — jazz-punk with DC pedigree and zero wasted notes.

spotify:track:2KJXQeZ2AKcaQiJjtqWaVJ.text: Cello-led ambient jazz — To March Is To Love drifts with purpose.

theme.name: The Ground Rules
paras: Edition one established the constraints the whole log runs on: nothing an algorithm would hand you. Every artist sits under 500k monthly listeners, and every track came out of the week's editorial writing.
Twenty tracks, twenty artists, one rule of thumb: if a recommendation engine already knows you want it, it doesn't make the log. Obscurity isn't the goal — discovery is. Obscurity is just the gate.

lanes_note: Week 1 predates the lane architecture (v2, 2026-08-29). Tracks are marked 'unlaned' deliberately: no scene/wildcard lanes existed; do not infer any.
